---
title: "Code from files: Python"
jupyter: python3
---

Ways to bring code that lives in `.py` files into a document. Each section
says what it shows and what it runs.

## Include shortcode inside a code cell

The file's text becomes the cell's code before anything runs: it is shown
and executed like code typed in the cell.

```{python}
{{< include _code/helpers.py >}}
```

```{python}
moving_average([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
```

## Import it as a module

The usual way in projects: only the import is shown.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_code")
from helpers import GREETING, moving_average
GREETING
```

## Run a script

`%run` (IPython) runs the whole file; its variables stay defined.

```{python}
%run _code/script.py
result
```

```{python}
exec(open("_code/script.py").read())
```

## Show a file without running it

```{python}
#| eval: false
{{< include _code/script.py >}}
```

## `file:` cell option

knitr reads the cell's code from `file:`; this checks what Jupyter does with it.

```{python}
#| file: _code/script.py
```
